title: Console nudge v1 scope: activation checklist + 2 banners (feature-flagged)
creator: Henry Cho
body:
## Context
We’re running the lifecycle growth experiments sprint focused on lifting activation (first successful production-like inference call) and early retention. This ticket defines the **v1 scope** of console nudges that ship behind a feature flag, with explicit acceptance criteria + rollout plan.

Owners / partners:
- PM (Console): Marissa Cole
- Activation milestone PM: Henry Cho
- Telemetry requirements: Paula Mendes
- Design: Tessa Morgan / Kenji Nakamura / Alicia Perez
- Eng: Chloe Martin (Console), Jada Williams / Jin Woo Park (experimentation), Logan Wright (analytics)

Related docs:
- PRD: lifecycle growth experiments sprint (Confluence)
- Console nudges spec (Confluence)
- Event taxonomy: activation/retention (Confluence)
- Experiment framework + guardrails (Confluence)

## Goals
1) Reduce time-to-first-success by guiding new self-serve users through the minimum required setup.
2) Increase completion of higher-intent early milestones (streaming enabled, dashboard viewed) without adding noise for already-activated users.
3) Ensure all nudges are measurable and safe (guardrails + easy rollback).

## Non-goals (v1)
- No major IA changes to Console navigation.
- No multi-step walkthrough modal or tours.
- No credits/incentives surfaced in console (covered by separate policy / experiments).
- No localization beyond en-US (but copy must be written to be localization-friendly).

## Scope (v1)
### A) Activation checklist component (feature-flagged)
Placement: Console home/dashboard for new users (first 14 days) and/or any workspace that has not hit activation.

Checklist steps (v1):
1. **Create API key** (deep link to API Keys settings)
2. **Make your first request** (deep link to Quickstart / “Try it” panel or docs)
3. **Enable streaming** (deep link to streaming docs + example snippet; completion based on first_streaming_success)
4. **View latency & cost** (deep link to dashboard tab; completion based on dashboard_viewed)

Behavior:
- Shows up only if user/workspace has NOT met activation definition (see “Activation definition” below).
- Each step shows: title, 1-line helper text, CTA button, and completion state.
- Completion state must be driven by events (not client-only local state).
- Checklist can be dismissed; dismissal persists for that user for 7 days (but does not count as completion).

### B) Banner #1: “You’re one step away” (post-key, pre-success)
Purpose: When users created a key but haven’t gotten a successful response, guide them to a minimal known-good request and troubleshooting.

Trigger (v1):
- Show if api_key_created happened AND no first_request_success within 30 minutes.
- Suppress if user has already hit activation.
- Frequency cap: max 1 impression per user per 24h.

CTA (v1):
- Primary: “Copy a working curl” (links to quickstart section anchored to curl)
- Secondary: “Troubleshoot auth errors” (links to troubleshooting section)

### C) Banner #2: “See your cost/latency” (post-success, pre-dashboard)
Purpose: Encourage users to look at the latency/cost breakdown after they’ve succeeded, to reinforce value + drive return.

Trigger (v1):
- Show if first_request_success happened AND no dashboard_viewed within 24 hours.
- Suppress if dashboard_viewed already occurred.
- Frequency cap: max 1 impression per user per 48h.

CTA (v1):
- Primary: “Open dashboards” (links to latency/cost dashboard)

## Activation definition (for suppression + experiment primary metric)
For purposes of *suppressing* onboarding nudges in console, treat “activated” as:
- **first_request_success** (first 2xx completion) for any of chat/text generation/embeddings endpoint.

Notes:
- Streaming success is a higher-intent follow-on milestone and is in the checklist but is not required to be considered activated.
- We will still track first_streaming_success and dashboard_viewed as secondary milestones.

## Instrumentation requirements (must-have)
All nudges must emit:
- nudge_impression (properties: nudge_id, variant_id, placement, user_id/workspace_id, is_activated, days_since_signup)
- nudge_click (properties: nudge_id, cta_id, destination)
- nudge_dismiss (where applicable)

Checklist must also emit:
- checklist_step_click (step_id)
- checklist_step_complete (step_id, completion_source_event)

Attribution requirements:
- CTA destinations must preserve UTMs where relevant (emails/retargeting may drive users back into console).

## Experimentation / flagging
- All nudges behind a single top-level feature flag: `console_onboarding_nudges_v1`.
- Experiment assignment handled via the console experiment middleware (ENG-2842) with sticky bucketing and holdout support.
- Default initial ramp: 10% of eligible users in week 1, then 50% if guardrails clean.

Eligibility (v1):
- New self-serve workspaces created after the sprint start date.
- Exclude enterprise contracts / Dedicated and Private orgs for v1 (avoid confusing buyers with different onboarding paths).

## Acceptance criteria
### Functional
- [ ] Checklist renders in dashboard for eligible users when flag is on.
- [ ] Checklist does not render for users who have already activated.
- [ ] Banner #1 triggers only in the defined window (post-key, pre-success) and respects frequency cap.
- [ ] Banner #2 triggers only in the defined window (post-success, pre-dashboard) and respects frequency cap.
- [ ] Dismissal works and persists (7 days) without breaking eligibility logic.
- [ ] CTAs route to correct console paths (no 404s) and open in the same tab.

### Measurement
- [ ] All impressions/clicks/dismissals emit correct events with required properties.
- [ ] Checklist completion is driven by canonical activation events (not manually toggled).

### Quality / performance
- [ ] No measurable regression in console page load/TTI (guardrail: <50ms p95 increase on dashboard route in sampled users; exact measurement method per Eng).
- [ ] Nudge rendering must fail safe (if telemetry endpoints fail, UI still loads; nudges can be hidden).

### Safety / rollback
- [ ] Turning off the feature flag fully disables checklist + both banners without redeploy.
- [ ] Holdout group remains unexposed.

## Rollout plan
1) Ship behind flag to staging + internal dogfood (Redwood employees) for 48h.
2) Prod ramp to 10% eligible users.
3) Check guardrails daily (unsubscribe spikes are email-side; console-side guardrails = support-link clicks, error banner clicks, console errors, perf).
4) If stable for 72h, ramp to 50%.
5) End of sprint: decide keep/iterate/rollback based on activation delta + qualitative support feedback.

## QA plan (minimum)
- Verify all trigger states with synthetic users:
  - brand new user (no key)
  - key created, no successful request
  - successful request, no dashboard view
  - already activated prior to exposure
- Verify frequency caps by manipulating timestamps in test env.
- Verify event payloads in analytics debug stream.

## Open questions
1) Should we key suppression/eligibility off user, workspace, or org? Proposal: workspace-level activation, user-level dismissal.
2) Should Banner #1 trigger after N errors rather than time-based? (Defer to v2; v1 is time-based to keep scope tight.)
3) Do we want a third banner for “Invite a teammate” post-dashboard? (Out of scope for v1.)

## Definition of done
- Feature shipped behind flag with acceptance criteria met
- Design sign-off on final copy + accessibility checklist
- Dashboards can slice by exposure vs holdout (ENG-2845)
comments: 2025-01-14 — Henry Cho: Created ticket to lock scope for v1. Goal is to keep this to checklist + 2 banners max to avoid thrash during sprint launch.

2025-01-15 — Kenji Nakamura (Design): Confirmed checklist placement preference = dashboard top-right module (collapsible). Will ensure keyboard focus order + contrast meets our standards; will follow up with DES-188.

2025-01-16 — Paula Mendes: Please ensure activation suppression uses canonical events (api_key_created, first_request_success, dashboard_viewed, first_streaming_success). Avoid client-only state; we need joinable exposure logs for analysis.

2025-01-17 — Chloe Martin (Eng): Feasible behind one flag. Need ENG-2842 for assignment + ENG-2843 for UI plumbing. Request: keep trigger logic server-derived (events) to avoid complex client polling.

2025-01-20 — Marissa Cole: Locked activation definition for suppression = first_request_success (2xx). Streaming remains secondary. Updated acceptance criteria to require frequency caps and dismissal persistence.
2025-01-22 — Jada Williams: Added note that flag-off must fully remove UI and event emission. We’ve been burned by partial disabling (events still firing).

2025-02-03 — Marissa Cole: Marking Done. Scope shipped behind `console_onboarding_nudges_v1` in console-2025.02; rollout to 10% started with daily guardrail checks. Any iteration requests should go to PM-416 backlog after readout.
